Actual Article Body:
Story one of ten today, about five minutes for the lot

Albanese warned Shoebridge that attacking Labor helps the far-right.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese warned the new Greens leader David Shoebridge yesterday that challenging Labor plays into far-right hands. When asked about Shoebridge's appointment, Albanese said it was concerning that the Greens chose to target Labor rather than the rising far-right party.

Albanese compared Shoebridge's approach to that of Adam Bandt and Max Chandler-Mather, who lost their seats in May's election. Albanese's quick public response signals Labor's anxiety about the Greens' shift toward more confrontational politics.

The government would prefer a cooperative Greens, despite having failed to slow One Nation's growth. Shoebridge has declared the Greens intend to replace Labor as the left-wing force in Australian politics.
